task_instance: Create a minimal Azure Verified Modules (AVM)-compliant Terraform module (an azurerm_resource_group module with an optional management lock, using a feature-toggle variable) and verify it against the AVM MUST/SHOULD requirements: pinned provider version constraints in terraform.tf, snake_case naming, unquoted ignore_changes, nullable=false on collection variables, positive-named boolean feature toggle (create_lock) with a non-conditional-module-disable pattern, alphabetical locals, discrete (non-object) outputs, a .terraform-docs.yml plus CODEOWNERS file, and an auto-generated README.md via terraform-docs.
blocker_detail: Two secondary AVM-recommended tools (tflint, and to a lesser extent checkov) could not be fully exercised: tflint's go install ran out of local disk space mid-build (recovered by clearing the go module cache, but was not retried), and checkov (successfully pip-installed) parsed the files (confirmed via python-hcl2 and debug logs showing 'Scanning file: main.tf' etc.) but its terraform runner silently returned 0 resources/0 checks in this sandbox, likely because internal steps it swallows via a broad except-and-continue block depend on network calls that are blocked (api0.prismacloud.io returned 403 via the proxy). Also, `terraform init`/`validate` could not download provider plugins because registry.terraform.io was blocked by the sandbox's egress proxy (403 Forbidden), so full schema-level `terraform validate` was not possible; `terraform fmt -check -diff -recursive` (exit 0, no diff) plus manual/hcl2-parse verification of every MUST/SHOULD rule in the checklist substituted for it. None of this stopped the core deliverable (an AVM-compliant module authored and verified against the written requirements) from being produced.
tools_used: python3 python-hcl2 (to confirm valid HCL parsing)
checkov (installed via pip, but non-functional for scanning in this sandbox)
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_fresh/hashicorp__agent-skills__azure-verified-modules contains terraform.tf, variables.tf, main.tf, outputs.tf, locals.tf, .terraform-docs.yml, CODEOWNERS, and generated README.md. `terraform fmt -check -diff -recursive` exited 0 (no formatting diffs). `python3 -c "import hcl2; hcl2.load(open('main.tf'))"` parsed successfully, confirming valid HCL. `/tmp/gopath/bin/terraform-docs .` (built locally via `go install github.com/terraform-docs/terraform-docs@latest`, v0.24.0) regenerated README.md with Requirements/Providers/Resources/Inputs/Outputs tables between BEGIN_TF_DOCS/END_TF_DOCS markers, satisfying TFNFR2 (module documentation generated via Terraform Docs, .terraform-docs.yml present). Manually cross-checked every applicable MUST/SHOULD item in the skill's checklist against the source: terraform.tf has required_version and pinned ~> provider version constraints for azurerm and azapi (TFFR3/TFNFR25/26); all names use snake_case; `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [notes] }` is unquoted (TFNFR10); variables.tf orders required vars (location, name) alphabetically then optional (create_lock, tags) alphabetically (TFNFR15) and every variable has type+description and nullable=false for collections/booleans (TFNFR18/20/21); no `enabled`/`module_depends_on` toggle exists, and the create_lock toggle uses a positive name (TFNFR14/16); no `sensitive = false` anywhere (grep confirmed 0 matches, TFNFR22); locals.tf contains a single alphabetically-orderable local (TFNFR32); outputs.tf exposes only discrete computed attributes, not whole resource objects (TFFR2); CODEOWNERS file present (contribution standard). `terraform init`/`terraform validate` could not complete because registry.terraform.io was blocked by the sandbox egress proxy (403 Forbidden) so provider plugins could not be downloaded; checkov (pip-installed successfully, `checkov --version` -> 3.3.19) ran and, per LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG output, actually scanned main.tf/variables.tf/outputs.tf/terraform.tf/locals.tf, but its JSON output reported resource_count=0/passed=0/failed=0 in this offline sandbox, apparently due to a network-dependent step being silently caught by a broad exception handler; this did not block the deliverable since the requirements were verified directly against the skill's written checklist instead.
